body_text:
Harlan,

Good running into you at the AME roundtable last week — really enjoyed hearing how Ferris is tackling changeover times on the stamping line. I've spent the last few years doing exactly that kind of work with manufacturers your size (Meridian Castings, Halberd Packaging among them), usually landing 15-25% reductions in changeover without new capex.

If it'd be useful, I'd love to grab 30 minutes and hear more about what's slowing you down on the floor. No pitch, just a conversation — I'll bring a couple of the case studies I mentioned.

Let me know what your July looks like.

Best,
Evelyn

snippet: Evelyn, Before I put together a number for the Stratus predictive-maintenance piece, I want to make sure I understand what's actually in scope. Is this just the vibration-sensor da
body_text:
Evelyn,

Before I put together a number for the Stratus predictive-maintenance piece, I want to make sure I understand what's actually in scope. Is this just the vibration-sensor data cleanup and a baseline anomaly-detection model, or are you also expecting me to build out the dashboard layer? Those are very different engagements — the first is maybe 60 hours, the second is closer to 150.

Also, do we know yet whether Stratus is even going to sign? I don't want to block time on my calendar for a deal that's still in proposal.

Anil

subject: Re: Stratus data workstream — scoping question
snippet: Anil, Fair questions. Scope is the first piece only — vibration-sensor data cleanup and a baseline anomaly-detection model, not the dashboard. If Stratus wants visualization later,
body_text:
Anil,

Fair questions. Scope is the first piece only — vibration-sensor data cleanup and a baseline anomaly-detection model, not the dashboard. If Stratus wants visualization later, that's a phase 2 conversation and a separate SOW; don't build anything toward it yet.

On timing: we're not signed. Owen McCabe is taking the proposal to his board on the 14th of next month, and my read is it's more likely than not, but "more likely than not" isn't a contract. I'm not asking you to hold calendar space yet — I'll give you two weeks' notice once ink is on paper, and I know that's tight, so I'd rather you keep your calendar honest than pretend otherwise.

For planning purposes: cap the engagement at 60 hours at your standard $220/hr, so $13,200, invoiced monthly against actuals. I'll want a short scope memo from you — half a page, what's in, what's out — so Owen's team has something concrete to sign off on alongside the SOW. Can you get me that by the 25th?

If this does sign, I want you leading the technical narrative in the kickoff call. Owen's ops team is skeptical of black-box models, and you're better at explaining the guts of it than I am.

Talk soon,
Evelyn

snippet: Owen, Attached is the full proposal — I wanted to get this to you tonight rather than wait until tomorrow, since I know Thursday is coming up fast. A few notes to help you walk you
body_text:
Owen,

Attached is the full proposal — I wanted to get this to you tonight rather than wait until tomorrow, since I know Thursday is coming up fast. A few notes to help you walk your board through it.

The core engagement is a 14-week operations diagnostic and improvement program across your Denver and Grand Junction plants, focused on the three things you flagged when we first talked: changeover time on the CNC lines, the predictive-maintenance gap that's driving unplanned downtime, and the supply-chain visibility problem that's been masking your true on-time-delivery number. Fixed fee of $340,000, billed in three milestone payments tied to the diagnostic readout, the improvement roadmap, and the implementation kickoff.

On the predictive-maintenance piece specifically — that's where Anil Bose comes in. He's a data scientist I subcontract with regularly, PhD in applied statistics, and he'll be doing the vibration-sensor data work directly, not delegating it to a junior analyst the way some of the bigger firms would. I think that matters given how skeptical your ops team was on our first call about anything "AI-flavored."

Team structure: I'm leading the engagement and will be on-site for the diagnostic weeks and the final readout. Ana Restrepo, my Principal, runs day-to-day delivery and will effectively be your point of contact between my visits — she's excellent and has run engagements of this size before. Kyle Brenner supports on the supply-chain workstream.

Reference-wise, I mentioned Bob Vandergriff at Meridian Castings on our call — I'm sending a separate note connecting you two directly so you can ask him anything you want about what it's actually like to work with us, warts and all. I'd rather you hear the honest version from a client than a polished one from me.

Timeline: if you can get a signed SOW to me by August 1st, we can start the diagnostic phase the week of August 10th and have the roadmap in your hands before your Q4 planning cycle starts, which I know matters to you given the capex conversations you'll be having in October.

Happy to jump on a call before or after the board meeting if it's useful to have me answer questions directly, live. Otherwise, I'll have this in your inbox with plenty of time to prep tonight.

Good luck Thursday — I think this is a strong case, and I think you know that too.

Evelyn Thorne
President, Thorne & Cadwell Advisory
312-555-0148
evelyn.thorne@thornecadwell.com

Diane,

Thanks for the detailed rundown and for your patience while I thought this through properly instead of giving you a quick no.

I don't think we're the right fit for this one. A single-plant scheduling fix at the scope and budget you've described ($8,500 fixed fee) doesn't let me staff it the way I'd want to — either I do it myself and it pulls me off larger commitments, or I put a junior consultant on it without enough of my oversight to feel good about the result. Neither is fair to you.

Two firms worth calling: Halstrom Operations Group does exactly this kind of focused scheduling work and does it well, and there's an independent consultant, Ray Petrucci, who used to be at a firm like ours and now takes on smaller engagements solo. Happy to make an introduction to either if useful.

Appreciate you thinking of us, and hope the project goes well.

Evelyn Thorne
President, Thorne & Cadwell Advisory

subject: Q3 pipeline & staffing review
snippet: Gordon, Wanted to get you a real picture of where things stand before we're both pulled into back-to-back client weeks. Attached is the pipeline summary, but here's the narrative v
body_text:
Gordon,

Wanted to get you a real picture of where things stand before we're both pulled into back-to-back client weeks. Attached is the pipeline summary, but here's the narrative version.

Meridian phase 2 is signed — $175K fixed fee, net-45, kickoff happened the 27th. Ana's running it day-to-day and I'm stepping back to a supervisory role after this week, which I need to actually do this time and not just say I'm doing. Phase 1 taught me I can't be both the rainmaker and the hands-on delivery lead on every account simultaneously, and Meridian is our biggest client — I'd rather protect that relationship by giving Ana real ownership than keep my fingerprints on everything.

Stratus is effectively closed — verbal yes from Owen's board, SOW finalizing with Terrence on a liability-cap redline, $340K fixed fee, diagnostic starting week of August 10th. This is the biggest new-logo win we've had since I started tracking it, and Anil Bose is doing the sensor-data work directly rather than delegating, which matters for how we position ourselves against the bigger firms on anything AI-adjacent.

Halberd is smaller but has scope-crept from 120 to 165 hours — I've sent a change order for the overage rather than eat it, which Lucia accepted without pushback. Good sign for the relationship, less good sign that our original scoping was too tight; Ana and I should talk about how we're estimating discovery-heavy engagements.

Ridgefield collections: invoice #10412, $18,400, still open at 90+ days. I sent Marta a direct note two weeks ago asking for payment by the 19th. If that date slips, I want to loop Terrence in before it gets adversarial — Marta's a friend of the firm even if her AP department is slow.

On staffing: I think we need to move on the fifth-consultant hire now, not in Q4 like we discussed. Between Meridian, Stratus ramping up, and whatever Halberd turns into, Ana and Kyle are both going to be stretched thin by September, and I don't want either of them burning out the way I did in year two. I've got a candidate interviewing Thursday — Marcus Ohene, six years at a firm doing similar manufacturing ops work, strong references from two people I trust — will fill you in after.

I know the fifth hire is a real cost before we've banked a dollar of Stratus revenue, and I don't want to pretend that risk away. But I'd rather grow into the work a quarter early than watch Ana or Kyle burn out trying to cover it, and then lose one of them to a client who poaches them once they're this good.

Let's find 30 minutes this week to talk through the hiring number and whether we're comfortable committing to it before Stratus revenue actually lands. I'd like to have a decision before I sit down with the Ohene candidate Thursday, so I'm not making promises I can't back up.

Evelyn

subject: Utilization, and why I keep bugging you about timesheets
snippet: Team, Quick note on something that's been nagging at me, and I'd rather say it plainly than keep dropping hints in Monday standups. July utilization across the firm was 68%. Target
body_text:
Team,

Quick note on something that's been nagging at me, and I'd rather say it plainly than keep dropping hints in Monday standups.

July utilization across the firm was 68%. Target is 78-80% for a firm our size to actually make the economics work — below that and we're either underpricing engagements or overstaffing them, and right now it's a bit of both. Ana and Kyle are both over 85%, which is genuinely too high and part of why I'm pulling myself back into a supervisory role on Meridian instead of running it day-to-day. Fiona, you're closer to 55%, partly timing, partly that Ridgefield and Halberd haven't kept you as busy as I'd like — that changes fast once Stratus kicks off, so don't read this as a complaint about you specifically.

The bigger issue is timesheet accuracy. I know it's the most annoying part of the job, and I know I am, personally, the worst offender — Sheila can confirm I'm usually three days late entering my own hours, which is a bad example to set while also asking everyone else to be diligent about it. I'm going to fix that on my end starting this week, timesheets entered same-day, no exceptions, and I'd ask the same of everyone else.

Here's why it actually matters beyond bookkeeping: every fixed-fee engagement we scope depends on knowing what similar work actually costs us in hours, not what we guessed it would cost. Halberd is a good example — we scoped it at 120 hours based on a rough gut-check, and it's at 165 and climbing, which means either our historical data was thin or nobody trusted it. Accurate time data going forward means better proposals, which means better margins, which is directly connected to whether we can afford the fifth-consultant hire I've been talking about for two quarters and am finally moving on this month.

I'm not trying to turn this into a big-firm bureaucracy exercise. I just want us pricing our time as if it's worth what it's worth, which means actually knowing what things cost. Ten people is small enough that we can still fix this with a plain email instead of buying software for it, so let's not overbuild the solution either.

Sheila — can you send a utilization breakdown by person, monthly, starting with July? I want it as a standing agenda item at Monday standup going forward, not a once-a-quarter surprise when Gordon and I are trying to close the books.

One more thing while I have everyone's attention: if you're consistently over 85%, tell me. I'd rather hear "I'm underwater" in a Tuesday message than find out in an exit interview. We're hiring a fifth consultant partly because of this exact conversation, and I want the hire to actually land before anyone burns out waiting for it.

Thanks for reading this far. Back to it.

Evelyn

meta.action_summary: Evelyn committed to entering her own timesheets same-day going forward, and asked Sheila for a monthly utilization breakdown.
